Suggest keyword merges

Source: R/keyword_review.R
suggest_merges.Rd

Finds pairs of keywords that may name the same concept, so that they can be judged by [ask_ai()] and by you in [review_sheet()]. Nothing is merged here. Use it on data that [keywords_clean()] has already cleaned.

A pair is suggested when the two keywords differ by

  • **spelling**: one or two letters (`BEHAVIOR CHANGE` / `BEHAVIOUR CHANGE`), never in numbers (`WEB 2.0` / `WEB 3.0`) or in short words (`AI` / `AR`);

  • **word order** (`DATA ANALYSIS` / `ANALYSIS OF DATA`);

  • **word ending** (`SOCIAL NETWORK` / `SOCIAL NETWORKING`);

  • **acronym**: one is the other's initials (`RNN` / `RECURRENT NEURAL NETWORK`), at most five long forms per acronym;

  • **meaning**: the two mean nearly the same (`HUMAN-COMPUTER INTERFACE` / `HUMAN-MACHINE INTERFACE`), by a `cosine` of at least 0.9 between their Sentence-BERT embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, through the sbert package). A narrower term (`CHATBOT` / `SMART CHATBOT`) is not suggested this way.

Look-alikes such as `MEDIATION` / `MEDITATION` are suggested on purpose: telling them apart is the reviewer's job. Every pair gets a `cosine`, how close the two are in meaning, and the pairs closest in meaning come first: look-alikes with different meanings (`ONTOLOGY` / `ONCOLOGY`, 0.26) sink to the bottom. The embeddings cannot read acronyms, so acronym pairs score low whether right or wrong; and they barely see word order, so `TEXT TO SPEECH` / `SPEECH TO TEXT` scores 0.97. The cosine orders the pairs; [ask_ai()] and you decide them.

Usage

suggest_merges(data, columns = "DE", skip = NULL, meaning = TRUE)

Arguments

data

Your papers, one row each: usually `as.data.frame(keywords_clean(...))`, or the [keywords_clean()] result. A `TI` column, if present, supplies example titles. A [institutions_clean()] result reviews institution names instead (column `AU_UN`): two institutions OpenAlex identified are never paired, and the OpenAlex name is the suggested one.

columns

The keyword columns. Default `"DE"`, or `"AU_UN"` for a [institutions_clean()] result.

skip

Review sheets from earlier rounds: pairs decided there are not suggested again.

meaning

Compare meanings with Sentence-BERT (`TRUE`, the default): adds the `meaning` pairs and the `cosine` that orders all pairs. Needs the sbert package and its model. With `FALSE`, `cosine` is empty and the pairs touching most papers come first.

Value

A `saqr_proposals` object. Print it for an overview. `as.data.frame(x)` gives one row per pair, the closest in meaning first: `pair` (its number), `keyword` (the suggested name), `variant`, `decision` (`check` until [ask_ai()] fills it), `found_by`, `keyword_papers`, `variant_papers`, `cosine` (-1 to 1), and the AI's `ai_verdict`, `ai_name`, `ai_confidence`, `ai_reason` (empty until [ask_ai()]). `as.data.frame(x, what = "evidence")` gives, per `pair`: `column`, `together` (papers listing both: a hint that they differ), `shared_keywords` (share of co-keywords in common), `similarity` (of the spelling, 0 to 1), `example_keyword`, `example_variant` (titles) and `ai_model`. `summary()` counts the pairs per `found_by`.

Errors

Raises `saqrmisc_bad_input` for a missing or non-character column, or a `meaning` that is not `TRUE` or `FALSE`; `saqrmisc_missing_package` when `meaning = TRUE` and sbert is not installed.

References

Reimers, N., & Gurevych, I. (2019). Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings using Siamese BERT-networks. *EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019*, 3982-3992. doi:10.18653/v1/D19-1410

See also

[ask_ai()], [review_sheet()], [review_report()], [keywords_clean()]

Examples

papers <- data.frame(
  TI = c("Coaching for behavior change", "Behaviour change at work"),
  DE = c("BEHAVIOR CHANGE; SOCIAL NETWORK", "BEHAVIOUR CHANGE; SOCIAL NETWORKING")
)
merges <- suggest_merges(papers, meaning = requireNamespace("sbert", quietly = TRUE))
#> Error: Model 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2' is not installed. Run model_download("all-MiniLM-L6-v2") once, or set options(sbert.download = TRUE) to allow this script to download it.
merges
#> Error: object 'merges' not found
as.data.frame(merges)
#> Error: object 'merges' not found
